fields.statement: QA at da0068fa7, hands-on with the built binary against the real published feeds: built rhiza stamped v0.1.1-main.5+aaa1111 into a scratch Rhiza root (isolated HOME), daemon set rhiza.daemon.autoUpdate latest (accepted; 'bogus' rejected with 'must be off or main or latest or release'), ran rhiza daemon --max-runs 0. It logged 'auto-update latest: installed v0.1.1-main.12+1f9c3a7 (was v0.1.1-main.5+aaa1111)' then 'binary changed, re-executing'; the executable's sha256 changed and rhiza version reported v0.1.1-main.12+1f9c3a7. Rebuilt stamped v0.1.1-main.12+1f9c3a7: the daemon ran 25s, logged no install, the executable was unchanged. (The re-exec'd published build predates this change and rejects the latest value, as expected for a pre-feature build.) Scoped tests: go test ./internal/daemon -run ChannelUpdate and ./internal/release pass; ./internal/api -run TestDaemonAutoUpdate tests all PASS, the package's root-state guard intermittently flags usage.live.json, which the VM's live root daemon rewrites every few seconds (the pre-existing TestDaemonAutoUpdateSetting alone trips it too).

QA at da0068fa7, hands-on with the built binary against the real published release feed (v0.1.0 release, v0.1.1-main.12 incremental): in a scratch Rhiza root with rhiza.daemon.autoUpdate=release, rhiza daemon --max-runs 0 built as v0.0.9 logged 'auto-update release: installed v0.1.0 (was v0.0.9)', re-executed, and rhiza version then reported v0.1.0. Built as v0.1.0, v0.1.0-5-gabc1234 and v0.1.1-main.5+aaa1111, each daemon ran 25s, installed nothing and left the executable byte-identical: the release channel ignores the newer incremental build and never downgrades an incremental build to the release. go test ./internal/api -run TestDaemonAutoUpdateRelease passes.
